transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi Dr. Smith. Nice to meet you too. 

Um, I'm here because... well, I keep having these nights where I eat an amount of food that honestly scares me. Like, I’ll start with just some leftovers after I finish grading papers for the day, but then I can't stop. I end up going through cereal, crackers, peanut butter... basically whatever snacks I packed for my classroom. It's just getting really out of hand.
After these episodes of eating, do you ever do anything to try and make up for it, such as vomiting, using laxatives, or exercising excessively?

I don't throw up or take laxatives or anything like that. But I do try to make up for it in other ways. 

Usually, after one of those bad nights, I’ll tell myself I’m just not allowed to eat breakfast or lunch at school the next day. And then... well, I’ll go out on the trail and run or walk for hours, or I'll force myself to do extra yoga. I just keep pushing myself to work out even when I’m completely shaky and exhausted.
Do you feel that these episodes of skipping meals and exercising for hours are driven by a strong desire to prevent weight gain or change your body shape?

Yes, that's exactly it. It's really all about my weight and how I look. 

Um... honestly, if I look even a little softer around my stomach, or if my pants feel tight right before a staff meeting, I just feel like I’ve failed at everything. It doesn't even matter how well my students are doing or how prepared I am for my classes. If my body is changing or my clothes don't fit perfectly, none of that other stuff matters to me, and I just feel this huge need to fix it by working out or not eating.
Could you tell me your current height and weight?

Um, I actually don't know my exact weight right now. I haven't stepped on a scale in a while... I kind of avoid looking at them because seeing the number just makes me spiral. And as for my height, I'm honestly not completely sure either. I haven't been measured in a really long time.
When you look in the mirror or catch a glimpse of yourself, would you describe your current body frame as being significantly underweight or emaciated?

No, definitely not. Um... I wouldn't say I look underweight at all. I certainly don't look emaciated. When I look in the mirror, I just see... well, I see areas that I still need to fix or work on, but I definitely don't look too thin or anything like that.
Over the past three months, how many times a week on average would you say these episodes of eating a large amount of food occur?

Um, over the past three months... well, for the past few months, there has rarely been a week without at least one night where I eat far more than I meant to. Honestly, it usually happens a lot more than just once. 

And then... the next day, I just try to make up for it. I'll usually do that by not eating at all while I'm at school, or I'll push myself through a really long walk or do extra yoga when I get home to try and fix it.
During these episodes where you eat a large amount of food, do you feel like you are unable to stop eating or unable to control how much you are eating?

Yes, absolutely. Um, once I start, it really feels like the reasonable, teacher part of me is just watching from the outside. I'm in my head saying, 'Joan, stop,' but I just... I can't. My hands just keep opening things and putting food in my mouth, and I don't stop until I'm completely, painfully full.
